items.note: The prompt opens with the choice between keeping Postgres with pgvector and moving to a dedicated vector database.
It gives about 5 million embeddings at 1536 dimensions, growing about 1 million per quarter.
It says the team already runs Postgres 16 on AWS RDS.
It sets the budget at under $500 per month and checks cost against it in the scan and the table.
It says the system is multi-tenant, so every query must filter by tenant_id, and the deep dive covers how each option does this.
It caps the comparison at 4 options including pgvector, says so more than once, and makes the cap part of the stop condition.
It asks for a comparison table plus one clear recommendation, with extra sections for when the recommendation would change and a source list.
It asks for sources from the last 12 months and says any older source must be flagged.
It asks for a wide scan first, then a ranking and a deep dive on the top 2.
